I am an old woman of eighty years, and this small plot behind my house is where I plant my cocoyam and cassava like my mother taught me. I have no money for the chemical fertilizer they sell in town, and my eyes and back cannot manage much heavy work anymore, so I put the ash from my cooking fire and some goat droppings on the soil. My grandchildren help me when they come from school, and my daughter-in-law helps with the weeding because I cannot bend for long.
